tldr: Harry pushed back on picking a database (Postgres/SQL) before there is a design, since the product briefing is a couple of weeks away.
Speaker 1 said the AI-generated plan was a rough exploratory deep dive, not a decision, and that nothing is committed.
Both agreed the US data-residency point is the one actionable item: the GCP region is fixed when the project is created, so it should go into the project request now.

Harry argued for the right tool for the job and showed that most of Fuse runs on separate Mongo instances. Speaker 1 said that shifts their view, since their Mongo problems may come from config rather than the technology.
They plan an informal system design session later today, once Speaker 1 is free after their call, which ends around 10.
decisions: Treat the database choice as open: no decision until there is a design, and no design until the product briefing.
Feed the US-based GCP region requirement into the project creation request, because the region can't be changed afterwards.
Hold a system design session later today.

actions.text: Ping Harry after about 10:00 once free from the DPD call to agree a time for the system design session.
Take Speaker 1 through a system design session, covering Fuse's database-per-service setup and what happens if a single database dies.
Send Speaker 1 reading on database storage and retrieval (chapters 2, 3 and 5 of the book he showed).
Read the recommended chapters on storage and retrieval.
Feed the US region requirement into the GCP project creation request, working with Ronnie.

questions: Which database fits the new system (Postgres/SQL, Mongo, AlloyDB or something else) once the design is known?
What data from Speaker 1's area is needed, and in what capacity, for the new build? This depends on the product briefing.
Is the carrier data still file-based, with zip-code-based downloads, or moving to API carriers? This affects whether one central source of truth is needed.
If a single central database serves everything, what happens when it fails, and how is that avoided?
Backend language: Go or TypeScript? Speaker 1 is happy with either and leans towards Go.
